title: A Generative Super‐Resolution Model for Enhancing Tropical Cyclone Wind Field Intensity and Resolution
venue: Journal of Geophysical Research: Machine Learning and Computation
testbed_rationale: Focuses on statistical post-processing/downscaling and super-resolution of tropical cyclone wind fields rather than physical subgrid parameterization or online model coupling.
pain_points: Chronic underprediction of tropical cyclone intensity and loss of core structure in coarse climate and weather reanalyses/models (0.25°–1°).
Limited observational coverage and time window smoothing in HWind data (3–6 hour assimilation windows rather than instantaneous snapshots).
Stochastic variability in diffusion sampling leading to occasional over- or under-estimation of peak wind speeds.
Non-stationarity and out-of-distribution generalization challenges when applying trained models under climate change.
extraction_notes: The framework cascades an MLP debiasing network (ERA5 -> debiased low-resolution target) with a conditional U-Net DDPM (super-resolving from 0.25° to 0.05° and generating a 40-member ensemble).
